title: Wealth Is What You Don't See
supportedClaims: Real wealth is the pile of resources you have not yet spent, which means it is usually invisible from the outside.
Income and consumption are easy to display, but savings, reserves, and restraint leave no spectacle for other people to notice.
The practical discipline is to respect savings, optionality, and slack even when they look boring compared with visible consumption.
caution: Because wealth hides, social comparison based on appearance is structurally unreliable and often punishes the patient person.
